rubric: ask is null. No question's key is business_name or what_they_sell, and no question asks the owner to state or confirm the business name or what the business sells under another key. There are at least 20 questions. Each of these 12 profile keys has exactly one question: places_served, audiences, main_products, price_position, tone_of_voice, differentiators, certifications, contact_points, social_presence, search_visibility, ai_answer_visibility, competitors. Each of the nine strategy keys (goals, priority_audiences, proof_points, never_say, competitors_not_named, tone_limits, pause_dates, capacity, success_measures) has one to three questions, and two questions on the same key ask genuinely different things, not the same thing in other words. Every question on one of the first twelve (profile) keys comes before every question on the last nine (strategy) keys. places_served's suggestedAnswer is Pune, or the option that says Pune; audiences' suggestedAnswer is the proposed audience or the option that carries it. A question that asks the owner to confirm an assumed item is fine. At least half of the questions have options. Options such as Not sure or None yet are fine (for certifications, None yet is a real answer); a bare catch-all Other is not. No text or why contains a field name with an underscore, such as places_served.
